newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money rates steady, demand low.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money rates steady, demand low.

text.p: Croatian money market rates were unchanged on Thursday amid dwindling demand, as banks accounts were full ahead of monthly salary payments, dealers said.

"There is a lot of money on offer as banks don't need many interbank loans now," one dealer said. "But we expect both the amount of money in supply and on the accounts to fall because of salary and pension payments starting now."
Some 40 million kuna were left in surplus on the supply side.
By mid-morning, trade totalled 14 million kuna, half of which was call money at a steady 10.5 percent.

Dealers said a growing supply of kuna on offer boosted the volume of term loans. The latter were granted at rates ranging between 11 percent for five and seven day funds and 18 percent for two-month borrowings.
The total amount of kuna funds on banks' accounts was slightly lower at 413 million kuna on Wednesday evening.

Overnight trade on Thursday totalled 17.2 million of which 2.2 million was sought by one bank with a shortfall and the rest went to another bank to maintain its mandatory reserves. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
